newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria needs $70 mln to secure this year's crop.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria needs $70 mln to secure this year's crop.

text.p: Bulgaria, in the throes of a grave economic crisis, seeks $70 million to pay for fertilisers and pesticides needed for cultivation of this year's grain crop, the Bulgarian Agricultural Chamber(BAC) said.

Battling an acute grain shortage after last year's poor harvest and uncontrolled exports two years ago depleted supplies, Bulgaria faces even a poorer harvest this year, if it fails provide funds for cultivation of crops.

"Bulgaria needs at least $70 million for fertilisers and pesticides for the autumn and spring crops otherwise it will suffer even greater grain crisis later this year," BAC spokesman Borislav Gergov told a news conference.
Bulgaria sowed 1.5 million hectares of wheat and barley so far up from 1.27 million hectares in the previous year. The country plans to sow 550 000 ha with maize this spring.

"These areas are enough to cover domestic consumption, but the planned yield of up to 330 kilograms per decare (0.1 ha) could be reached only if the crops are properly cultivated with the needed fertilisers and other chemicals," said Gergov.
Earlier this week officials said that Bulgaria's bread wheat supplies will end in the next 15 to 20 days and the state reserve currently holds only 30 percent of its usual supplies.
The caretaker government, in office since last week, has set up a special Grain Crisis Solution Council led by interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski, due to meet late on Wednesday.
The cash-strapped Balkan country also hopes to win funding from the European Union and other international lending institutions and governments, agriculture minister Roumen Hristov said recently.
